guarantees.claim: For all i in [0, NumRegsKey-1], hw2reg.key_share0[i].d is continuously assigned to key_init_q[0][i] and hw2reg.key_share1[i].d to key_init_q[1][i].

formal.consequent: forall i (0 <= i < NumRegsKey) : hw2reg.key_share0[i].d == key_init_q[0][i] && hw2reg.key_share1[i].d == key_init_q[1][i]

formal_sketch.consequent: forall i (0 <= i < NumRegsKey) : hw2reg.key_share0[i].d == key_init_q[0][i] && hw2reg.key_share1[i].d == key_init_q[1][i]

assumptions.claim: key_init_q[0] and key_init_q[1] hold correctly loaded and protected AES key shares before this block drives them to hw2reg inputs.
assumptions.cond: whenever the design relies on the transferred key material for encryption/decryption
assumptions.risk: If key_init_q contains corrupted, uninitialized, or attacker-controlled values, the hw2reg key registers will latch invalid key material, leading to broken encryption or potential key leakage through side channels or read paths.

formal_sketch.antecedent: whenever the design relies on the transferred key material for encryption/decryption

uncertain_points.claim: If NumRegsKey is configured to 0, the for-loop body does not execute, leaving hw2reg.key_share0.d and key_share1.d undriven.
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven register inputs could capture random or previous values, possibly injecting uncontrolled key material into the AES datapath and violating security properties.

security_implications: The key_share0/1.d signals directly expose AES key shares from key_init_q onto combinational net hw2reg. If the hw2reg interface allows any read path (e.g., CSR reads) or if these nets are not physically cleared after use, secret key material may be observable. Additionally, the lack of a write-enable qualifier inside this block means key data is continuously driven, increasing the window for probing attacks. The block assumes that key_init_q already contains valid shares; any failure in earlier key loading or masking will propagate directly to the register inputs.
